name: Coverflow / Card-Deck Carousel
summary: Cards travel a perspective arc with real 3D rotation: the active card faces flat at center while flanking cards tilt away, shrink, dim, and step back — the album-coverflow grammar, plus its siblings (stacked fanned decks that shuffle forward, centered-focus testimonial tracks). The premium tell is genuine dimensional tilt and shadow craft, not a flat slide.

composition: One active card is ALWAYS the focal anchor: biggest, brightest, forward; every sibling exists to frame it.
Generous whitespace around the track lets the 3D arc read cleanly — coverflow dies in cramped layouts.
Variants share one grammar: coverflow arc, fanned deck shuffle, centered-focus scale track — pick per content type (media, photos, quotes).
layering: Depth via overlapping stacks: active card top plane, neighbors stepped back with reduced scale, opacity, and slight blur.
Soft drop/contact shadows ground each card on a light backdrop — shadow quality is where cheap implementations fail.
Cards are physical objects: consistent corner radius, thickness illusion via shadow, no weightless floating.
lighting: Soft ambient light with gentle contact shadows under each card; no glows — the premium feel comes from clean shadow craft.
Light backdrop keeps the register friendly; a dark variant trades shadows for rim separation.
typography: Crisp sans for UI/labels; a warm serif for quote content on testimonial variants.
Oversized decorative quotation marks can serve as type ornaments on quote cards.

rules: Light neutral canvas + one warm accent family; chroma concentrated in the card imagery, chrome kept pale.
Cards must share a tonal register — the arc presents them as one collection.

easing: Smooth ease-in-out with a gentle settle; cards rotate on a fixed perspective so travel CURVES rather than sliding flat.
Scale, opacity, and tilt animate in lockstep — desynced properties break the physicality.
pacing: Comfortable mid-tempo advances (~600-900ms), interaction-driven, no perpetual auto-drift.
Deck-shuffle variants snap slightly faster — a card dealt, not a page turned.
choreography: Center-focus choreography: the incoming card grows and comes forward while flanks shrink, dim, and rotate away simultaneously.
Every sibling moves on every advance — the whole track breathes, not just the active card.

gapNotes: True 3D card tilt is native to our renderer (easier than the DOM's matrix3d), but soft CONTACT SHADOWS under floating cards need the R1 cinematic floor (W-PHOTO) — without them cards float weightlessly.
Same missing 'carousel driver' primitive as filmstrip-3d-carousel: the N-cards-on-an-arc state machine must be hand-built per instance.

whenToUse: Small curated sets (3-9 items) where each deserves individual attention: testimonials, case studies, featured products, team members.
Friendly, warm, consumer registers — this is the most approachable carousel grammar in the corpus.
whenNotToUse: Dense catalogs needing many visible items and fast scanning — coverflow deliberately hides/shrinks non-active items.
When items are text-heavy: tilted cards make flanking content illegible by design.

notes: One carousel mechanic per surface — the cluster exists because carousels are the most-repeated pattern in template galleries.

antiRepetition.notes: Same cluster as filmstrip-3d-carousel, bento-grid-slider, swatch-variant-swap.

sources.title: Carousel Design Templates WordPress Pack
sources.motionEvidence: Founder monitor session, live demo: page scrolled through the full anthology; coverflow arc, stacked-deck shuffle, and centered-focus testimonial track each advanced through multiple states; matrix3d perspective tilt confirmed from the motion (side cards rotating, not just scaling).

exemplars.promptSummary: Five glossy rounded cards fanned on a curved arc in perspective, center card upright and sharp, side cards tilted/receding with depth blur, reflections on a dark glass floor with soft contact shadows — the coverflow depth read.
exemplars.notes: ORIGINAL render (Replicate black-forest-labs/flux-2-pro, ~$0.06). Subject deliberately distinct from any analyzed source template. Illustrates the family aesthetic target (palette/composition/lighting); does NOT demonstrate runtime motion or in-engine execution.
